Asset type: independent full-resolution chapter master for a deluxe illustrated edition of Pliny the Elder, Naturalis Historia, Book VIII chapter 50, “Goats and Their Propagation”
Primary request: Treat the chapter’s reproduction, medicine, vision, anatomy and behavioral claims as transmitted ancient testimony, never modern animal-care advice. Visualize only Mutianus’s nonviolent anecdote of two goats solving a passage on a narrow bridge, emphasizing calm cooperation and intelligence rather than danger or spectacle.
Scene/backdrop: A steep, almost bird’s-eye view into a Cilician greenstone ravine at cool malachite morning. One short, narrow but sound ancient stone footbridge is fully visible in the center with both complete abutments and low flat walking surface. Far below, a small turquoise torrent emerges from one dark rock opening and disappears into a second dark rock opening; BOTH openings and the ENTIRE visible watercourse are fully enclosed inside the image, surrounded on every side by a wide continuous band of dry rock and ferns. No water, reflection, spray, or wet channel may touch any canvas edge.
Subject: EXACTLY TWO goats total and no people. On the bridge, exactly ONE complete tawny hornless goat lies calmly lengthwise, body relaxed and head lifted; exactly ONE complete charcoal-gray horned goat carefully steps over the lying goat, placing its hooves on the clear bridge stones beyond the other’s body rather than on the animal. Their heads face opposite directions, making the encounter legible. Both animals are healthy, unrestrained and mutually attentive. No other animal anywhere.
Style/medium: original Plinian zoological folio painted across warm fibrous aged vellum; iron-gall contours, exceptionally fine cross-hatching and stipple, dry-brush abrasion; deep malachite and muted verdigris vegetation, charcoal-green stone, contained turquoise/faded-lapis water, tawny ochre and lampblack coats, a few pale mineral highlights; ancient, timeless, materially rough yet polished in draftsmanship.
Composition/framing: one continuous landscape 3:2 scene at exactly 1536x1024. The bridge runs diagonally from lower left toward upper right through the central sixty percent; the two goat silhouettes remain visually separate and the contained water glows far below as a small internal accent. Show every horn tip, ear, muzzle, torso, leg, hoof and tail of both goats, including the lying goat’s four folded legs; show the whole bridge, both abutments, both rock openings, full water boundary, ferns and all contact shadows. Maintain generous dry-land margins and breathing room from every edge. No element may form a panel or internal frame.
Historical/ethical framing: the episode is a literary observation of problem-solving, not a recommended handling method, demonstration, forced stunt, or claim of species ranking.
Output intent: one opaque RGB/sRGB 1536x1024 master, no alpha.
Avoid: mating, pregnancy, birth, kid, herd, human, handler, rope, collar, horn pulling, beard pulling, eye puncture, blood, liver, medical treatment, sacrifice, olive damage, fall, panic, hoof pressing on another goat, cruelty, cliff-edge peril, bridge collapse, third goat, duplicated limb, fused anatomy, cropped horn/hoof/tail/bridge, water touching an image edge, text, letters, numerals, inscription, pseudo-writing, caption, label, signature, logo, watermark, visible sheet/page edge, border, internal frame, panel, split scene, collage, repeated crop, modern object, photography, photorealism, glossy CGI, or smooth digital rendering.
rejectedAttempts.reason: The first bridge scene let the turquoise watercourse continue through the lower boundary and allowed the bridge approach to run into the image edge, violating both the contained-water and complete-structure framing gates. The rejected built-in original remains byte-identically preserved under evidence/history.

chapters.title: THE HOG
chapters.exactFinalPrompt:
Use case: historical-scene
Asset type: independent full-resolution chapter master for a deluxe illustrated edition of Pliny the Elder, Naturalis Historia, Book VIII chapter 51, “The Hog”
Primary request: Treat Pliny’s reproductive timings, disease signs, sacrifice rules, fasting, surgery, force-feeding, slaughter and banqueting as transmitted ancient testimony, never modern husbandry or medical advice. Visualize only two humane observations: hogs delight in mud and can recognize the familiar voice of their keeper.
Scene/backdrop: A spacious Roman-era orchard enclosure under soft pewter morning light, seen from a low wide viewpoint. At center lies one shallow irregular oval mud wallow, fully contained with a complete raised dry-earth rim; a broad band of dry straw, grass and packed earth separates every part of the wallow and every damp mark from all four canvas edges. One complete simple open wooden gate stands in the right-middle distance with both posts, hinges and lower corners visible. No trough, feast, market, ship, altar, surgical structure, or water.
Subject/action: EXACTLY FOUR swine total: exactly ONE complete healthy adult sow and exactly THREE complete healthy piglets, each piglet clearly separate and individually countable. The sow has just stepped out of the shallow wallow onto dry straw and turns her head attentively toward a familiar call; all four legs and hooves and her complete curled tail remain visible. The three piglets stand separately around the dry outer rim—one sniffing earth, one looking toward the sow, one taking a small step toward the gate—so no body overlaps or hides another. EXACTLY ONE complete adult keeper total stands just inside the open gate in plausible Roman rural dress, empty hands open near the chest as if calling softly, without food, tool, rope or contact. No other person or animal anywhere.
Style/medium: original Plinian zoological folio painted across warm fibrous aged vellum; iron-gall contours, fine cross-hatching, stipple and dry-brush abrasion; rich red-umber and dusty rose hides, lampblack mud shadow, muted orchard verdigris, faded-lapis pewter light, ochre straw and one quiet madder cloth accent; ancient, timeless, materially rough yet polished in draftsmanship.
Composition/framing: one coherent landscape 3:2 master, exactly 1536x1024. Use a low crescent arrangement: complete sow left-center, three piglets spaced across the wallow rim, open gate and keeper at right, with pale orchard air and empty ground providing negative space. Show every ear, snout, eye, torso, leg, cloven hoof and complete curled tail of all four swine; show the keeper’s full head, both empty hands, garment hem, legs and sandals; the entire wallow and dry rim; and every part of the complete gate. Keep all subjects and damp ground well inside generous margins.
Historical/ethical framing: an ordinary scene of animal pleasure and learned recognition, without calling swine brutish or reducing them to food. No claim about reproduction, health, sacrifice, surgery, feeding, flavor, or moral worth is endorsed.
Output intent: one opaque RGB/sRGB 1536x1024 master, no alpha.
Avoid: fifth pig, boar, wild boar, mating, pregnancy, birth, nursing, cannibalism, corpse, disease, pulled bristle, blood, cut, spaying, suspension, fasting, force-feeding, figs, wine, slaughter, meat, banquet, sacrifice, theft, sinking ship, crowd, food reward, trough, rope, collar, stick, knife, tool, touching, restraint, cruelty, dehumanization, pig partly submerged, hidden legs, overlapping pig bodies, clipped snout/hoof/tail/gate/person, wallow or moisture touching an edge, text, letters, numerals, inscription, pseudo-writing, caption, label, signature, logo, watermark, visible sheet/page edge, border, internal frame, panel, split scene, collage, repeated crop, modern object, photography, photorealism, glossy CGI, or smooth digital rendering.
chapters.visualQaNotes: Inspected at native 1536x1024 resolution. Exactly one complete sow, three distinct complete piglets, and one complete empty-handed keeper form the orchard scene. The irregular wallow and all damp ground are fully enclosed by dry earth and straw, while the entire open gate, every snout, leg, hoof, curled tail, hand and sandal remain internal. Learned recognition and ordinary pleasure replace breeding, disease, surgery, forced feeding, slaughter, food reduction, text, panel, border, or clipped focal subject. Canonical bytes were verified identical to the accepted built-in original.
